issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Stock.add(String) as returning void, but the template and solution implement Stock.add(String) to return int (the new quantity). This return-type mismatch can confuse students: if they follow the UML and implement add as void, their code will not match the provided template signature and may not compile or integrate with the provided Stock class behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the problem statement UML with the code by changing the UML signature to +add(String): int and update any textual descriptions to indicate that add returns the updated quantity. Alternatively, change the template and solution to make add return void, but keeping the current int return is preferable to preserve the implemented behavior; therefore update the UML and documentation to +add(String): int.
